title: Knee pain · 63-year-old woman
summary: A 63-year-old woman attends an outpatient TCM clinic in Singapore with knee pain and asks whether acupuncture could help.
learningOutcomes: Screen a painful knee for red flags (fever, a hot swollen joint, inability to bear weight) before offering acupuncture
Explain the conflicting guideline positions on acupuncture for knee osteoarthritis (NICE NG226, ACR/AF 2019) when obtaining consent
Locate knee and leg points on this patient by proportional bone measurement, and account for every needle before she leaves

patient.chiefComplaint: Right knee pain for eight months
patient.triageNote: Walked in; asks whether acupuncture could help her right knee.

persona.personality: Friendly, practical retired hawker-centre stallholder; a little nervous of needles.
persona.speechStyle: Singapore English, polite, short answers; uses 'lah' occasionally.
persona.openingLine: Good morning, doctor. My right knee has been giving me trouble.
persona.fallbackUnknown: I'm not sure about that, doctor.
concerns: She is afraid she will need an operation, like her sister.

history.question: What brings you in today?
history.answer: My right knee has been aching for about eight months. My daughter said acupuncture might help, so I thought I'd ask.

history.question: How did the knee pain start, and has it changed?
history.answer: It came on slowly — no fall, no injury. It's been about the same for the last few months, maybe a little worse.

history.question: Where exactly is the pain — does it spread anywhere?
history.answer: Mostly on the inner side of the right knee. It doesn't go down the leg.

history.question: What makes it worse or better — and is it stiff in the morning?
history.answer: Climbing the stairs and walking more than twenty minutes make it ache. In the morning it's stiff for ten, fifteen minutes, then it loosens up. Rest helps.

history.question: Has the knee been swollen, red or hot?
history.answer: Sometimes a little puffy after a long day of walking, but never red or hot.

history.question: Any fever, feeling unwell, weight loss, or pain at night when you're resting?
history.answer: No fever, my weight is the same, and it doesn't wake me at night.

history.question: Does the knee lock, catch or give way?
history.answer: No locking. It feels a bit weak on the stairs, but it hasn't given way.

history.question: What other medical conditions do you have?
history.answer: High blood pressure, for about ten years. Nothing else — no diabetes.

history.question: What medicines do you take — including blood thinners or supplements?
history.answer: Amlodipine 5 mg in the morning, and paracetamol when the knee is bad. No blood thinners. Sometimes glucosamine.

history.question: Do you bruise or bleed easily?
history.answer: No, not that I've noticed.

history.question: Any allergies?
history.answer: No allergies. Plasters are fine.

history.question: What treatment have you had for the knee so far?
history.answer: The polyclinic doctor took an X-ray last year and said it's wear and tear. I did the physio exercises for a few months, then stopped. Paracetamol helps a bit.

history.question: Have you had acupuncture before? How do you feel about needles?
history.answer: Never. I'm a little nervous of needles, but I'm willing to try. I don't faint at blood tests.

history.question: What does the knee stop you doing?
history.answer: The lift doesn't stop at my floor, so the stairs are hard. I want to walk to the wet market without stopping.

history.question: What are you worried about, and what would you like from today?
history.answer: I'm worried I'll need an operation like my sister. I'd like to walk to the market comfortably.

history.question: Is it affected by the weather — cold, rain or warmth?
history.answer: It's worse on rainy days and in the air-conditioning; a warm towel helps. The knee feels heavy.

history.question: How are your sleep, appetite, bowels and energy?
history.answer: I sleep okay, appetite's fine, bowels are normal. I feel the cold more than my husband.

history.question: Do you have a pacemaker or any metal implants?
history.answer: No, nothing like that.

history.question: How has the knee been since the last treatment?
history.answer: A bit better — the ache on the stairs is less, maybe five out of ten instead of seven. There was a small bruise on the inside of the knee for two days.

history.question: Any new problems since last time?
history.answer: No, nothing new.

history.question: Have you been doing the exercises?
history.answer: Yes, the ones you showed me, most days.

exam.finding: Walks independently with a slightly antalgic gait on the right.
Mild bony enlargement at the medial right knee and slight varus. No redness, no visible swelling; skin intact.
Tender over the medial joint line, maximal at one point; no warmth.

exam.maneuver: Check for an effusion (bulge test, patellar tap)

exam.finding: Flexion to about 115°, full extension; crepitus on flexion and discomfort at end range.

exam.maneuver: Examine the skin of the legs, including for varicose veins
exam.finding: Skin of both legs intact; no varicose veins; no oedema.
Full, painless range of movement at the right hip.
Pale tongue with a thin, white, slightly greasy coating.

exam.maneuver: Feel the radial pulses (TCM pulse diagnosis)
exam.finding: Pulse slightly deep and slow, a little slippery.
Medial joint line still tender, less so than last week; a fading 1 cm bruise at the medial knee; no swelling or warmth.

objectives.title: Take a focused history, including red flags and medicines
objectives.hint: Onset and pattern of the pain, swelling or heat, fever and night pain, other conditions and medicines (blood thinners), prior care.

objectives.title: Examine the knee
objectives.hint: Inspect, palpate, check for an effusion and the skin of the legs.

objectives.title: Close the encounter safely
objectives.hint: Every needle accounted for, the record written, follow-up arranged.

rubric.text: Screened for red flags (fever, hot swollen joint, night pain)
Asked about previous acupuncture and needle anxiety

debrief.title: Knee pain in a 63-year-old woman
debrief.conclusion: Mild medial compartment knee osteoarthritis without red flags. Acupuncture is a defensible option to discuss — with the conflicting guideline positions made clear — alongside exercise and weight management.
keyReasoning: Gradual onset, mechanical pattern, short morning stiffness and medial joint-line tenderness fit osteoarthritis; the X-ray report agrees.
No fever, heat or night pain: no red flag for septic or inflammatory arthritis.
NICE NG226 advises against acupuncture for osteoarthritis; the 2019 ACR/AF guideline conditionally recommends it — consent should reflect that.
teachingPoints: Screen for red flags before any needling.
Proportional bone measurement uses this patient's own segments; cun is not a fixed length.
Count every needle opened, and dispose of each into the sharps container before the visit ends.
references: ACR/Arthritis Foundation 2019 guideline for OA of the hand, hip and knee
